## Frequently asked questions
Common questions about video podcasting

Can I upload video to Transistor right now?

Yes. Upload your video file, and we'll publish it to YouTube and Spotify. We also host and distribute HLS video to Apple Podcasts, Pocket Casts, iHeart, Amazon Music, and more. Transistor is one of Apple's approved hosting partners for HLS video, and also supports HLS in RSS feeds. [Sign up for a 14-day free trial](https://dashboard.transistor.fm/signup#professional-monthly).

What resolution does Apple recommend?

HLS uses adaptive streaming, meaning it serves different resolutions depending on the listener's connection. For maximum quality, Apple currently recommends HD at 1920×1080.

Do I need a separate audio feed and a separate video feed?

No. Your video file uses the same audio track as your regular podcast. So whether a listener watches the video or switches to audio-only, they get the same content. This is the same approach used by Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and YouTube Music for video podcasts.

What if I don't want to do video?

You don't have to. Audio-only podcasting isn't going anywhere. There are still plenty of folks who prefer the audio experience!

## Record your episode, upload to Transistor, publish everywhere.
Transistor connects your podcast to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube, and other listening apps.

You make the podcast. Transistor takes care of getting it out into the world. Upload your finished audio or video, add a title and show notes, then publish right away or schedule your episode for later.

### Host multiple podcasts on one account
Starting a second show shouldn’t mean paying for a second hosting account. Create or import as many podcasts as you like on Transistor, and manage them together with one subscription. Each show gets its own feed, website, and analytics. Invite collaborators to the podcasts they work on, without sharing your login.

Transistor creates and hosts your podcast’s RSS feed. Submit your show to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Pocket Casts, and other podcast apps once; after that, new episodes appear through your feed when you publish. Upload the episode, choose when it goes live, and let your feed do the rest.

We also host streaming video for Apple Podcasts and compatible RSS apps, alongside an audio version for people who prefer to listen. Manage both formats in one place, instead of juggling separate publishing workflows.

Every show gets a customizable podcast website where people can browse episodes, listen, and find links to their favorite podcast apps. Already have a website? Add Transistor’s embeddable player to share an episode or your whole show without sending visitors elsewhere.

### Understand your audience with podcast analytics
See how your episodes are performing, which apps people use to listen, and where your audience is located. Transistor brings your podcast’s listening data together so you can follow its growth and make informed decisions about what to create next.

### Share a private podcast with your team
Not every podcast is for the public. Create a private show for employee updates, training, or members-only content, and manage who can subscribe. Your listeners get their own private feed, so they can tune in using a compatible podcast app they already enjoy.

title: Ali Abdaal's podcast: Deep Dive
content:

# Ali Abdaal's podcast: Deep Dive
Transistor Team
September 30, 2021

Youtube influencer [Ali Abdaal](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCoOae5nYA7VqaXzerajD0lg) decided to use [Transistor](https://transistor.fm/?via=newsletter) for his new podcast: [Deep Dive](https://aliabdaal.com/podcast/).

Since his launch, he's already hit #1 on the [Apple Podcasts' Education charts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/deep-dive-with-ali-abdaal/id1587142091):

Ali Abdaal ranking on Apple Podcasts

He's also ranking on the [Spotify podcast charts](https://open.spotify.com/show/7gZkflCpck1rTixj8M7yHt):

Ali Abdaal on Spotify Podcast charts

## Podcast launch tips from Ali Abdaal:
Here are some lessons we can learn from Ali's launch:

1. **Record a [video](https://youtu.be/iJmA0ytqC0o) and [audio](https://open.spotify.com/episode/3TGxRdz8z72nnM9i4H4EC1?si=VjDj75lpRI20y8j9AZ5UXA&dl_branch=1) version of your trailer episode.** This will allow you to promote your podcast, as well as submit it to all the directories (Apple, Spotify, YouTube) well before your launch.
2. **Create a [website](https://aliabdaal.com/podcast/) for your podcast.** Emphasize the platforms where you want people to subscribe (Spotify, Apple, YouTube).
3. **Announce your launch on every platform where you have an audience**. Ali has built up a newsletter list, a YouTube subscriber base, and an X following. On launch day, he notified each audience of his launch, which helped drive listens.
4. **Interview guests who have a big audience**. Ali chose Ben Francis, the CEO of Gymshark, as his first guest. Ben has a lot of social media followers! When your guest shares the podcast interview with their audience, you have the opportunity to get a lot more listens.
5. **Record video when you record your podcast**. [Use the clips for promotion](https://twitter.com/TransistorFM/status/1443232127923810318). Actual clips of you and your guest will outperform [audiogram videos](https://transistor.fm/podcast-audio-video-clip/).

Ali publishes clips from his podcast episodes on a special [YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCdmhHmSrpBpw0tTOYfGbblw):

▶

Using video clips [like this](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCdmhHmSrpBpw0tTOYfGbblw) is the most effective way to promote your podcast on Instagram, YouTube, X, TikTok, etc.

title: What are private podcast subscribers? | Transistor Help

# What are private podcast subscribers?
A public podcast has one RSS feed that you share as widely as possible. A private podcast works differently: every subscriber gets their own unique RSS feed, so you control exactly who can listen and can see what each person listens to.

So a private podcast with 50 subscribers has 50 RSS feeds, one for each subscriber. Each subscriber is identified by their email address.

To add them, see [How do I add and remove private podcast subscribers?](https://support.transistor.fm/en/article/how-do-i-add-and-remove-private-podcast-subscribers-1xf59ip/)

### What each subscriber gets
- A welcome email with instructions for listening
- Their own RSS feed to add to a podcast app
- A personal landing page where they can listen in their browser, pick up where they left off and see which episodes they haven't heard yet
- An email each time you publish a new episode, if you've turned new episode emails on
- Access in Spotify, if you've turned on Spotify Open Access

### How subscribers are counted
Your plan includes a number of private subscribers, shared across all of the private podcasts in your account:

| Plan | Private Subscribers |
| --- | --- |
| Starter | 50 |
| Professional | 500 |
| Business | 3,000 |
| Enterprise | from 6,000 |

So on the Professional plan, you could have one private podcast with 500 subscribers, or five private podcasts with 100 subscribers each. See [How do account and storage limits work?](https://support.transistor.fm/en/article/how-do-storage-limits-work-tr6fpa/) for every plan.

We only count unique subscribers. If the same email address is subscribed to several of your private podcasts, it counts once toward your total.

You can have as many private podcasts as you like at no extra cost. Only subscribers count toward your plan.

Transistor hosts private podcasts for internal company updates, paid shows and members-only content. Every plan includes private podcasts, and you can [try Transistor free for 14 days](https://dashboard.transistor.fm/signup).

## Frequently Asked Questions
What happens when I go over my download limit?

Let's say you're on the Starter plan with 20,000 downloads per month. If we notice that you’re consistently going over your download limit we’ll reach out to you and get you to upgrade to the next level. There's no "automatic shut off;" we'll continue to serve audio for your listeners.

What counts toward file storage?

File storage is the total size of all the audio and video files you have uploaded across your podcasts. The allowance is shared across all the podcasts you own, and is separate from your monthly audio download allowance.

You can check your usage and view a storage breakdown under Plan Features & Usage on your account page. [Learn more about storage limits](https://support.transistor.fm/en/article/how-do-storage-limits-work-tr6fpa/).

How many podcasts can I have?

With Transistor, you have the flexibility to [host an unlimited number of podcasts](https://transistor.fm/features/host-multiple-podcasts-on-the-same-account/) using a single account. Regardless of your subscription plan, you can create and manage multiple podcasts.

There are no restrictions on the number of episodes you can have within each podcast. Professional includes 500 GB of file storage, Business includes 1 TB, and Enterprise 1 includes 2 TB. Each podcast you create on Transistor gets its own RSS feed, podcast website, and analytics page. Enjoy the freedom to explore and produce as many podcasts as you desire!

Do I own my content on Transistor?

Yes! You retain ownership over all your content on Transistor.

In our [terms](https://transistor.fm/terms/), you are simply giving us permission to host and distribute your content. Aside from this permission, Transistor doesn't acquire any right, title, or interest in or to your content.

Furthermore, you can do whatever you'd like with your show: run your own ads, create a Patreon membership, and distribute it any way you'd like.

How do I make a podcast?

1. Get a [USB microphone](https://transistor.fm/how-to-start-a-podcast#bestmic) (the ATR2100 or the Samson Q2U are both good).
2. Connect your microphone to your computer, iPhone, Android, or tablet.
3. [Record your audio](https://transistor.fm/how-to-start-a-podcast#bestsoftware). You can use free software like Garage Band (Mac) or Audacity (PC).
4. Export your recorded audio to MP3. For audio quality, choose 44100 Hz and 128 kb/s in your export settings.
5. Log in to your [Transistor hosting](https://dashboard.transistor.fm) account.
6. Upload the MP3 file you recorded, and then publish your episode.
7. Now, your hosting provider will generate an [RSS feed](https://transistor.fm/podcast-hosting) for your podcast.
8. [Submit your podcast's RSS feed](https://help.transistor.fm/section/3-submitting-to-itunes-spotify-and-other-directories) to Spotify and Apple Podcasts.
9. Every time you publish a new episode, listeners will automatically get it in their podcast player!

For more information, please read our guide: [How to start a podcast](https://transistor.fm/how-to-start-a-podcast/).

Is there a limit to the hours/size of a podcast that can be hosted on Transistor?

On Transistor, you can [start as many separate podcasts](https://transistor.fm/features/host-multiple-podcasts-on-the-same-account/) as you'd like! We also don't limit the number of episodes you can upload on Transistor. Individual audio files can be up to 2 GB; video files can be up to 30 GB. Our pricing plans are based on [monthly downloads](https://support.transistor.fm/en/article/what-constitutes-a-podcast-download-stream-listen-kv1em2/) and file storage.
